SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
WEDNESDAY - MAY 7, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD WEDNESDAY, MAY 7, 2025, 7:00
PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Mark E. Pulido.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Hong Lee (Asian-American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander Heritage Month).

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Eugene Japor expressed support for enhancements to the City’s Let Freedom Ring
  Celebration on July 4, 2026 to highlight the United States 250 th Anniversary and for the
  City’s participation in upcoming Los Angeles events, such as the Star Wars 50 th
  Anniversary Celebration in 2027 and the 2028 Olympics.

  Greta Manila expressed concern regarding parking enforcement in her neighborhood and
  requested enforcement be reinstated.

  Elmer Manila expressed concern and requested information regarding drone usage in his
  neighborhood.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding decreasing crime rates in the City and urged residents to
  remain vigilant. He also inquired regarding public art pieces and submitted a document
  for the record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are
  considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk.)
 City of Cerritos  Wednesday, May 7, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Joan Pylman expressed concern and requested information regarding the Del Amo Bridge
  replacement and traffic signal synchronization project.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to schedule an agenda report for
  City Council review and consideration of the Del Amo Bridge replacement and traffic
  signal synchronization project, inclusive of an updated project timeline.

  Randon Lane, Athens Services representative, provided an update regarding waste
  hauling services, billing, and communication with the City.

  Eugene Japor spoke in support of Athens Services customer service.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, April 21, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve the Monday, April 21,
  2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated May 7, 2025 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  May 7, 2025  $4,272,484.87 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.2. Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency
  dated May 7, 2025 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  May 7, 2025  $300.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for resealing windows at the Cerritos Library, Capital Project No.
  24209* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of
  the CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report
  associated with this item;

  2. Award a contract in the amount of $59,325.43 to Horizons Construction Company
  International, Inc. for Library Windows and Roof Repair, Project No. 24209, as
  permitted by the Cerritos Municipal Code and the City’s adopted Purchasing and
  Contracting Policy; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any necessary contracts,
  agreements, change orders, or amendments to complete the specified scope of work,
  consistent with the City’s Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

(minutes continue on the next page)

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to approve Mayor Pro Tem
  Johnson’s nomination listed below for a two-year term of service, through April 30, 2027
  (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Deepak “DJ” Jhaveri  Planning Commission

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to approve Mayor
  Yokoyama’s updated nominations for service appointments for his 2025-26 Mayoral term,
  as listed below (COUNCIL).

  City Council Internal Ad Hoc Working Groups
  Name  Liaisons
  Personnel  1. Johnson  2. Pulido
  Public Safety  1. Hong  2. Tse

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an informational hiring data report prepared pursuant to
  requirements established under Assembly Bill 2561 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Drew Schneider, Director of Administrative Services. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  Rogan Girard, President, AFSCME Local 619 (Union), spoke regarding improved
  communication between the Union and the City and expressed support for recently
  improved City employee recruitment efforts. He also stated the City should transfer the
  responsibility of payroll processing back to the City’s Finance Division and requested
  improvements to succession planning and training. Additionally, he expressed concern
  regarding the impacts of having a large number of part-time staff, who are limited to
  working 960 hours each fiscal year and provided suggested improvements.

  Alma Griffin, Chief Steward, AFSCME Local 619 (Union), expressed concern regarding the
  impacts of having a large number of part-time staff, who are limited to working 960
  hours each fiscal year.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Pulido): Directed the City Manager to: 1. Schedule a closed session item,
  prior to the adoption of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Combined Financial Program (City
  Budget), to discuss an overview of the City’s contract with the AFSCME Local 619
  employee bargaining unit; and 2. Provide a copy of the subject contract to the City
  Council prior to agendizing this item.
Boards, Commissions, and Committee service appoi
  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Pulido, to refer this matter to the
  Personnel Ad Hoc Working Group (Johnson and Pulido) to review the new Alternate Work

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  At this juncture, Robert A. Lopez, City Manager, announced the recent hiring of Eric
  Cardoso, Library Services Manager, Lauren Vargas, Enterprise Services Manager, and
  Glenn Arnade, Marketing Administrator; and the recent promotion of Amy Thomas,
  Human Resources Manager, Jorge Martinez, Parks and Trees Superintendent, Jenny
  Mireles, Theater Patron Services Manager, and Steven Hart, Technical Administrator.

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider New and Old
Business Item 9D prior to consideration of Item 9C.

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational report on Cerritos Library card fees
  (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the next
  City Council/Successor meeting agenda (scheduled for 7:00 p.m., Thursday, May 22,
  2025).

  There were no members of the public who elected to speak on this item. There was no
  action taken on this item.

9D.  Review and consideration of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Preliminary Combined Financial
  Program for the City of Cerritos and the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment
  Agency (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Drew Schneider, Director of Administrative Services, and
  Peter Kemp, Finance and Budget Manager/City Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the three (3) written comments
  submitted for Item 9D, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the
  official record. Requests for copies of the written comment submitted for this meeting
  can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to direct the City Manager
  to include, with the consideration of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Annual Financial Program
  (City Budget), an allocation to fund the City’s acquisition and use of a federal lobbyist
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 0 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Hong

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to include, with the consideration
  of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Annual Financial Program (City Budget), information related to
  the fiscal impact of closing facilities in the Civic Center, including City Hall and Library,
  one day every other week, and/or one day every week.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to provide the City Council with a
  memorandum detailing funding requests the City has received from community
  organizations, for Fiscal Year 2025-26.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to direct the City Manager to
  include, with the consideration of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Annual Financial Program (City
  Budget), information related to cancellation of the annual Autumn Moon Festival and
  options to reimagine the event as a lantern festival in celebration of the Lunar New Year,
  to be held in February or March (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Tse
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Pulido, to direct the City Manager to
  include, with the consideration of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Annual Financial Program (City
  Budget), information related to cancellation of the Santa’s Holiday Float program and the
  scheduling of a one (1) day Santa’s Sleigh Day event (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Wednesday, May 7, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
